name: ADS1220IPWR
title: ADS1220: 24-bit, 2 kSPS, 4-input delta-sigma ADC with PGA, reference, IDACs and temperature sensor, SPI
summary: A low-power 24-bit delta-sigma ADC for small sensor signals such as thermocouples, RTDs, thermistors and bridges. A multiplexer gives two differential or four single-ended inputs into a PGA with gains of 1 to 128 (1 to 4 with the PGA bypassed for single-ended work), at 5 SPS to 2000 SPS with a single-cycle-settling filter that rejects 50 Hz and 60 Hz together at 20 SPS. It carries a 2.048 V reference, a 2 % oscillator, a 0.5 °C temperature sensor, two matched 10 µA to 1.5 mA current sources and a low-side bridge switch, and talks SPI mode 1. Supplies are 2.3 V to 5.5 V (or ±2.5 V analog), current is as low as 120 µA in duty-cycle mode, and it is specified from -40 °C to +125 °C in TSSOP-16 or 3.5 mm VQFN-16.
key_figures: 24 bits no missing codes; up to 20 bits effective
20 to 1000 SPS normal, 5 to 250 SPS duty-cycle, 40 to 2000 SPS turbo
NMRR 90 dB min at 20 SPS, both together
AVDD 2.3 V to 5.5 V, DVDD 2.3 V to 5.5 V
340 µA analog + 75 µA digital typ, normal mode gain 1 to 16

notes: All are active production parts, RoHS compliant. Package sizes: TSSOP 5.0 mm × 6.4 mm, VQFN 3.5 mm × 3.5 mm, both nominal and including leads.

circuits.title: Serial interface connection to a microcontroller
circuits.description: The converter on a single 3.3 V rail talking to a microcontroller's SPI port. Each of the five logic lines (CS, SCLK, DIN, DOUT/DRDY, DRDY) passes through a 47 Ω series resistor; a spare GPIO drives CS and a GPIO with interrupt watches DRDY. The microcontroller's DOUT goes to DIN and its DIN reads DOUT/DRDY. CLK is tied to digital ground so the internal oscillator runs. AVDD and DVDD each have a 0.1 µF capacitor, and the microcontroller's own supply has another. The analog inputs and reference pins are left unconnected.
notes: AVDD and DVDD both run from 3.3 V; AVSS and the AVDD capacitor return to analog ground, CLK, DGND and the DVDD capacitor to digital ground.

circuits.title: K-type thermocouple measurement, -200 °C to +1250 °C
circuits.description: A K-type thermocouple read between AIN0 and AIN1 at gain 32 with the internal 2.048 V reference, using the on-chip temperature sensor for the cold junction. RB2 pulls the AIN0 lead toward 3.3 V and RB1 pulls the AIN1 lead to ground, which centres the thermocouple near mid-supply inside the PGA's common-mode range and drives the reading to full scale if a lead breaks. RF1, RF2 and CDIF form a differential low-pass whose corner follows equation 16; CCM1 and CCM2, ten times smaller than CDIF, filter common-mode noise; RF1 and RF2 also limit input current under overvoltage. The thermocouple joins the board at an isothermal block close to the device. AVDD and DVDD run from 3.3 V with 0.1 µF each.
notes: RB1 and RB2 have no single value; typical values run from 1 MΩ to 50 MΩ.
Register settings: 00h = 0Ah, 01h = 04h, 02h = 10h, 03h = 00h.

circuits.title: Ratiometric 3-wire RTD measurement, -200 °C to +850 °C
circuits.description: A 3-wire Pt100 excited by both IDACs at 500 µA each: IDAC1 leaves AIN2 into the RTD's lead 1 and IDAC2 leaves AIN3 into lead 2. Both currents return through lead 3 and the 1.65 kΩ reference resistor RREF to ground, so the reference voltage across RREF is about 1.65 V and also sets the input common mode near mid-supply. Because the reference comes from the same currents, the code depends only on the ratio of RTD to RREF (equation 23), and with matched currents and equal lead resistances the lead drops cancel (equation 25). The RTD voltage is taken between AIN1 and AIN0 through RF1, RF2, CDIF1, CCM1 and CCM2; the reference reaches REFP0 and REFN0 through a matching filter RF3, RF4, CDIF2, CCM3, CCM4. Gain 8 gives ±206.25 mV full scale against the 195.5 mV the Pt100 gives at 850 °C.
notes: RF1 to RF4, CDIF1, CDIF2 and CCM1 to CCM4 have no fixed value; they are chosen by the thermocouple filter guidance, with the input and reference filter corners matched.
The leads RLEAD1 to RLEAD3 are the RTD's wiring, not parts.
Register settings: 00h = 66h, 01h = 04h, 02h = 55h, 03h = 70h.

circuits.title: Ratiometric 2-wire RTD measurement
circuits.description: The 2-wire form of the RTD circuit, with one IDAC. IDAC1 leaves AIN3, runs through lead 1, the RTD and lead 2, then through RREF to ground; the drop across RREF is the reference on REFP0 and REFN0. AIN1 and AIN0 sense the two ends of the wiring, so both lead resistances add to the measured value (equation 38) and can only be removed by calibration. With a single current through RREF the transfer is RRTD × Gain / RREF, twice that of the 3-wire circuit, and the reference and common-mode voltages are lower. Filters as in the 3-wire circuit.
notes: RF1 to RF4, CDIF1, CDIF2 and CCM1 to CCM4 have no fixed value; they are chosen by the thermocouple filter guidance, with the input and reference filter corners matched.

The leads RLEAD1 and RLEAD2 are the RTD's wiring, not parts. RREF carries the 3-wire design's value; with one IDAC the reference and common-mode voltages fall, and a larger RREF, or a larger current at lower gain, may be needed to keep the PGA common mode in range.

circuits.title: Ratiometric 4-wire RTD measurement
circuits.description: The 4-wire form with one IDAC. IDAC1 leaves AIN3, flows in on lead 1, through the RTD, out on lead 4 and through RREF to ground, where it sets the reference on REFP0 and REFN0. Leads 2 and 3 are a Kelvin pair carrying only input leakage to AIN1 and AIN0 through the input filter, so the measured voltage is the RTD's own and the lead resistance drops out. Transfer RRTD × Gain / RREF, as in the 2-wire form. Filters as in the 3-wire circuit.
notes: RF1 to RF4, CDIF1, CDIF2 and CCM1 to CCM4 have no fixed value; they are chosen by the thermocouple filter guidance, with the input and reference filter corners matched.
The leads RLEAD1 to RLEAD4 are the RTD's wiring, not parts.

circuits.title: Ratiometric resistive bridge (load cell) measurement
circuits.description: A 1 kg, 3 mV/V load cell excited from the 5 V analog supply, with its excitation used as the reference: the top of the bridge goes to AIN0/REFP1 and the bottom to AIN3/REFN1, so drift in the excitation cancels. The bottom of the bridge is switched to AVSS by the on-chip low-side switch, which closes on START/SYNC and opens on POWERDOWN when PSW = 1, cutting bridge current between conversions. The bridge outputs reach AIN1 and AIN2 through RF1, RF2, CDIF1, CCM1 and CCM2; CDIF2 across the reference limits reference noise, kept small so the measurement stays ratiometric. At gain 128 the ±15 mV full-load output fits inside the ±36 mV the PGA allows on 5 V (equation 40). AVDD is 5 V and DVDD 3.3 V, each with 0.1 µF.
notes: RF1, RF2, CDIF1, CDIF2, CCM1 and CCM2 have no fixed value.
B1.OUT+ is the bridge output wired to AIN1 (AINP) and B1.OUT- the one wired to AIN2 (AINN).
Register settings: 00h = 3Eh, 01h = 04h, 02h = 98h, 03h = 00h.

circuits.title: Supply decoupling, unipolar analog supply
circuits.description: AVDD and DVDD each on 3.3 V with a 0.1 µF ceramic capacitor placed close to the pin; AVSS and DGND go to ground, with analog and digital grounds joined close to the device. CLK connects to DGND when the internal oscillator is used.

circuits.title: Supply decoupling, bipolar analog supply

operation.text: A 24-bit delta-sigma converter: an input multiplexer, a low-noise PGA, a switched-capacitor modulator and a single-cycle-settling digital filter, with an internal 2.048 V reference, an internal oscillator, a temperature sensor, two matched current sources (IDACs) and a low-side power switch. Four 8-bit registers configure it and six commands drive it over a mode-1 SPI port.

MUX[3:0] picks four single-ended, two differential or mixed inputs. For single-ended settings AINN is switched to AVSS inside. It can also route (AVDD - AVSS)/4 or (VREFPx - VREFNx)/4 to the converter for monitoring, short both inputs to mid-supply for offset measurement, and connect either IDAC to any AINx, REFP0 or REFN0. ESD diodes to AVDD and AVSS guard every input; keep inputs within AVSS - 0.3 V to AVDD + 0.3 V or limit current with series resistors or Schottky clamps. Overdriving an unused input can disturb conversions on others.

Gains 1 to 128 come from a chopper-stabilized two-amplifier PGA followed by a switched-capacitor gain of up to 4 at the modulator input. The PGA input has an EMI filter (200 Ω and 25 pF per side, corner about 31.8 MHz). Each PGA amplifier output must stay 200 mV inside the rails, which limits the input common-mode range by gain and signal (equations 12 to 14). Worked example: AVDD 3.3 V, gain 16, VREF 2.5 V allows 1.45 V ≤ VCM ≤ 1.85 V at full scale, widening to 1.0 V to 2.3 V when the signal is held to ±0.1 V.

At gains 1, 2 and 4, PGA_BYPASS turns the PGA off, saving power and opening the input and common-mode range to AVSS - 0.1 V to AVDD + 0.1 V; a buffered switched-capacitor stage then gives the gain. Single-ended measurements against AVSS on a unipolar supply need the PGA bypassed. Gains above 4 always use the PGA; single-ended signals at those gains need a bipolar supply. High-impedance sources may still need an external buffer.

VREF[1:0] picks the internal 2.048 V reference (default), REFP0/REFN0, REFP1/REFN1 (shared with AIN0 and AIN3) or AVDD - AVSS. The internal reference settles in under 25 µs after power-up, wake-up or a switch from external. External reference inputs are buffered, so they draw little current; selecting one raises the analog supply current.

The internal oscillator runs when CLK is tied to DGND at power-up or reset. Two rising edges on CLK switch the device to the external clock; only a power cycle or RESET returns it to the internal oscillator. The modulator clock is fCLK/8 in turbo mode, fCLK/16 otherwise. Data rates and filter notches scale with the clock; the 50/60 Hz rejection figures need a 4.096 MHz external clock.

A linear-phase FIR filter that settles in one conversion. At 20 SPS (normal) and 5 SPS (duty-cycle) the 50/60[1:0] bits choose 50 Hz, 60 Hz or simultaneous 50 and 60 Hz rejection. The filter response repeats at multiples of fMOD, so content near fMOD aliases unless an external RC filter removes it; an RC corner at the data rate or up to ten times above it is a reasonable start.

In continuous mode the first conversion starts 210 tCLK (normal, duty-cycle) or 114 tCLK (turbo) after the last SCLK falling edge of START/SYNC. Single-shot times run from that edge to DRDY falling; with the internal oscillator add up to 50 µs (normal, duty-cycle) or 25 µs (turbo) for oscillator wake-up, which starts at the first SCLK rising edge of START/SYNC and is not always complete above 160 kHz (320 kHz turbo) SCLK.

Two matched IDACs, 10 µA to 1.5 mA set together by IDAC[2:0], each routed by I1MUX/I2MUX to any analog or REFP0/REFN0 pin, both may share a pin. Keep the pin voltage at or below AVDD - 0.9 V for rated accuracy. They take up to 200 µs to start: set the current first, then the routing. They stay on between single-shot conversions and are turned off by POWERDOWN. Enabling them draws extra bias current even unrouted, plus the output current when routed.

A 3.5 Ω switch from AIN3/REFN1 to AVSS. With PSW = 1 it closes on START/SYNC and opens on POWERDOWN, staying closed between single-shot conversions; PSW = 0 opens it at any time. It is open by default. Leave an unused AIN3/REFN1 floating so it cannot be shorted to AVSS by this switch.

BCS enables 10 µA sources, one into the selected AINP and one out of AINN. An open sensor then reads full scale; full scale can also mean overload or a missing reference, and near zero a short. The current varies about ±10 % and the mux adds series resistance, so a shorted sensor behind an RC filter may not read zero. Turn them off for precision readings.

MUX = 1101b converts about (AVDD - AVSS)/4 and MUX = 1100b about (VREFPx - VREFNx)/4 of the selected external pair; both use the internal reference with the PGA bypassed at gain 1 and give only a coarse figure.
MUX = 1110b shorts both PGA inputs to (AVDD + AVSS)/2. Store the reading taken in this state, averaged over several conversions to reduce noise, and subtract it from each later reading.

TS = 1 converts the internal temperature with the internal reference, ignoring register 0. The result is a 14-bit two's-complement value left-justified in the 24-bit word, 0.03125 °C per LSB: shift right by 10, then multiply (for a negative value, invert, add one and multiply by -0.03125 °C). Examples: 0960h is 75 °C, 3CE0h is -25 °C.

Power-up starts a reset of about 50 µs, after which the reference is settled and the interface is ready. Registers default to 00h (single-shot mode); the device makes one conversion and then idles, and DRDY falling marks it ready. Supplies may come up in any order within the input limits; ramp DVDD with or before AVDD, because until DVDD is up the low-side switch may short AIN3/REFN1 to AVSS. Ramps must be monotonic and no faster than 1 V per 50 µs. Wait about 50 µs after supplies settle before talking to it.

Single-shot (CM = 0): START/SYNC runs one conversion, then the oscillator and analog blocks (except the IDACs) power down. Any register write also starts a new conversion, restarting one in progress. Continuous (CM = 1): set CM then send START/SYNC; register writes restart the running conversion.

Normal: fMOD 256 kHz, 20 to 1000 SPS. Duty-cycle: normal-mode conversions at one in four cycles with sleep between, 5 to 250 SPS, noise like normal mode at four times the rate. Turbo: fMOD 512 kHz, 40 to 2000 SPS, more power and lower noise than normal mode at the same rate. Power-down: entered after the current conversion when POWERDOWN is sent; analog blocks, reference and IDACs off, switch open, about 400 nA typ; registers kept and commands accepted. START/SYNC wakes it in the selected conversion mode; a register write wakes it for one conversion.

SPI mode 1 (CPOL = 0, CPHA = 1): DIN is latched on SCLK falling edges and DOUT/DRDY changes on rising edges. CS high resets the interface and floats DOUT/DRDY; CS may be tied low on an unshared bus. DRDY falls when data are ready and returns high on the next SCLK rising edge; unread, it pulses high for 2 tMOD before the next result. With DRDYM = 1, DOUT/DRDY also falls with DRDY. An incomplete command is dropped after 14000 tMOD (28000 in turbo) so the next SCLK starts afresh; for RREG and WREG the register bytes count as part of the command.

24-bit two's complement, MSB first. Positive full scale reads 7FFFFFh and negative full scale 800000h; the output clips there. A single-ended signal uses only 000000h to 7FFFFFh, but offset can produce negative codes near 0 V.

RESET (06h) restores defaults; wait 50 µs + 32 tCLK before the next command. START/SYNC (08h) starts or restarts conversion and resets the filter. POWERDOWN (02h) powers down after the running conversion. RDATA (1xh) loads the latest result; if a conversion ends during the command byte, DRDY staying low after the read means the old result was sent. RREG (0010 rrnn) reads nn + 1 registers from rr; WREG (0100 rrnn) writes nn + 1 registers from rr, applied on the last SCLK falling edge.

When DRDY falls, clock out 24 bits on DOUT/DRDY with DIN held low; no RDATA is needed. Commands may be sent on any byte boundary while reading: WREG does not corrupt the read and restarts conversion with the new settings after the 32nd SCLK, while RREG or RDATA abort the read unless sent during the last byte. No command is decoded during an RDATA or RREG transfer until all its bytes are clocked.

SCLK, DIN and DOUT/DRDY can be shared with one CS per device; only the DRDY pin shows new data while CS is high. Without DRDY wired, set DRDYM = 1, drop CS and read the level of DOUT/DRDY: low means new data. This needs DOUT/DRDY high before CS rises, so send eight extra SCLKs with DIN low after each read.

Example for gain 16, continuous mode, 50/60 Hz rejection: wait at least 50 µs after power-up; set SPI mode 1; CS low; send RESET (06h); wait 50 µs + 32 tCLK; write WREG 43h with 08h, 04h, 10h, 00h; optionally read back with RREG 23h; send START/SYNC (08h); then on each DRDY falling edge clock out 24 bits. POWERDOWN (02h) stops conversions.

With a unipolar supply, single-ended signals need the PGA bypassed (gains 1 to 4); a 0 mA to 20 mA loop across 100 Ω can be read this way at gain 1 with the internal reference. Pseudo- and fully-differential signals work with the PGA on or off, keeping the PGA common-mode rules when it is on; a common mode near (AVSS + AVDD)/2 usually satisfies them. Bipolar signals need a bipolar supply such as ±2.5 V; a ±10 V signal can be divided down to within ±2.048 V. Signals above 2.048 V need an external reference, for example 5 V reference and AVDD = 5 V for 0 V to 5 V.

An unused analog or reference input may float or be tied to mid-supply or AVDD (AVSS works but leaks more); always leave AIN3/REFN1 floating if unused. Never float digital inputs: tie them to DVDD or DGND, CS to DGND if unused, CLK to DGND with the internal oscillator. Leave DRDY open or weakly pulled up to DVDD.
47 Ω in series with CS, SCLK, DIN, DOUT/DRDY and DRDY damp edges and overshoot and add some overvoltage protection; recheck SPI timing with the bus capacitance.

Bias resistors (1 MΩ to 50 MΩ) hold the thermocouple at mid-supply and detect a broken lead; keep their current low to avoid self-heating and lead drops. Keep filter resistors below 1 kΩ where possible, since input current through them adds offset; CDIF at least ten times CCM. 52.171 mV at 1250 °C with a -40 °C cold junction sets gain 32 (2.048 V / 52.171 mV = 39.3). Cold-junction compensation is done in the host: measure VTC, read the internal sensor, convert TCJ to an equivalent voltage, add and convert back with NIST tables. Good thermal contact between cold junction and package matters.

Choose the largest reference voltage that keeps the IDAC compliance and PGA common-mode limits; mid-supply is a good start. RREF stability sets the accuracy over time and temperature: ±10 ppm/°C or better, and a nearby value such as 1.62 kΩ or 1.69 kΩ works. With small, matched RF1 and RF2, IDAC1 can be routed to AIN1 and IDAC2 to AIN0, letting two 3-wire RTDs share one reference resistor.

Only REFN1 can be switched to AVSS by the low-side switch, so the bridge low side goes there for automatic power-down. A symmetrical bridge excited from the device supply meets the PGA common-mode range, but the PGA limits the usable input to ±[(AVDD - AVSS) - 0.4 V] / Gain rather than the full ±VREF / Gain.

Decouple AVDD, DVDD and (on a bipolar supply) AVSS with at least 0.1 µF low-ESR, low-ESL ceramic capacitors right at the pins. Avoid vias between capacitor and pin in very noisy systems; use several parallel vias to ground planes. Join analog and digital ground close to the device.

Keep analog parts apart from digital and RF parts and keep digital traces out of analog areas. A solid ground plane or fill matters more than split planes; if planes are split, join them near the device. Place a capacitor differentially across each input pair; AIN0/AIN1 and AIN2/AIN3 are the best pairs. Use C0G capacitors for the differential filters. For thermocouples, thermally isolate a copper area round the input connections to form a stable cold junction.
